scope: Partial human reconstruction of RH and unrestricted Dirichlet GRH, accepting the pinned Alpoge-Claude formal proof as correct. Version 0.50 adds 98 independently reviewed numbered claims, bringing the cumulative inventory to 3112. It completes arbitrary-coefficient test-ring descent, normalized theta points and every FrameOK field, uniform character seeds and much of the actual common marked frame, large-parameter Bessel nonvanishing and its universal return, the analytic final propagation step, and the full conditional global denominator export. No additional whole selected obligation is closed: 24 remain, comprising 17 class C and 7 class B, with 17 shared RH/GRH and 7 additional Dirichlet-GRH obligations. Full StepStatement, full simultaneous principal frames, the remaining common arithmetic frame and automorphy producers, actual ConclF families and other listed producers remain explicit. The existing full GLOBAL_LOCAL_GAIN closure is preserved. Claim counts are an inventory, not a completion percentage. No Lean build or kernel replay is claimed.
range_convention: All line numbers are one-based inclusive. Ranges may include trailing comments or namespace endings before the next declaration.
status_convention: Source translations retain their hypotheses. Derived alternatives have written mathematical proofs but have not been replayed in Lean. Remaining inputs have not been supplied with complete human proofs.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.
SP-C1.matching: Applied only to finite O modules whose finiteness is proved in the chapter. SP1 handles additive, not assumed O-linear, injections through finite cardinality. SP6 proves the norm-weighted length formula from these finite module facts.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C1.name: Noetherian formal series, complete quotients and henselian finite algebras
IX-C1.statement_used: Finite formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; quotients of a complete Noetherian local ring remain complete; a finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a finite product of local rings, so a finite domain is local.
IX-C1.matching: Used on the actual IsCO rings, the finite eigenvalue algebra C[b], and complete prime quotients. Integrality makes the origin evaluation land in O; uniqueness of the maximal ideal proves localness before reducing quotient labels. Successive approximation arguments are given directly.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion
IX-C2.statement_used: A locally projective morphism is proper; a quasi-compact morphism is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.
IX-C2.source: Stacks Project, Lemma29.44.5 tag01WC and Proposition26.20.6 tag01KF.
IX-C2.matching: The symplectic flag variety is explicitly a closed incidence/isotropy subvariety of a product of Grassmannians. The schematic closure of the actual generic flag is proper and surjects the integral base. A chosen K-point then extends over the given valuation ring. This does not assume smoothness, flatness or uniqueness of flags.

IX-C3.name: Weak Nullstellensatz
IX-C3.statement_used: Every nonzero finite-type algebra over an algebraically closed field has a rational closed point.
IX-C3.matching: Applied only to the nonzero finite-type invariant fibre. Nonzero follows from the weight-zero retraction before field extension. Full formal evaluation is justified separately using positive valuations and finite monomial decompositions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.
IX-C4.matching: Captures finitely many algebraic flag-basis entries in a single complete DVR inside the original V. Equal-characteristic purely inseparable extensions are handled separately by adjoining ell-power roots of a uniformizer over the perfect finite residue field; Milne is not misquoted as already proving that part.

IX-C5.name: Minkowski: no nontrivial everywhere-finite-unramified extension of Q
IX-C5.statement_used: A finite extension of Q unramified at every finite prime is Q.
IX-C5.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorem4.9, printedp72/PDFpage74.
IX-C5.matching: Applied to each finite continuous reduction of a powered character. The character is first shown trivial on every original inertia group, including ell. Separatedness is used only after these finite assertions. No assertion about arbitrary infinite unramified extensions is used.

IX-C6.name: Density theorem over an algebraically closed field
IX-C6.statement_used: The image of an algebra in the endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional simple module over an algebraically closed field is the full endomorphism algebra.
IX-C6.source: P.Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, January10,2011, Theorem2.5(i), p24; Section2.5 finite-dimensional algebra proof.
IX-C6.matching: Used only to turn simplicity on G_L back into the literal matrix-span Irr predicate. The finite-index semisimplicity, self-twist construction, injective characteristic-zero transport and distinct residual-character contradiction are proved in IX10.

KX-LOCAL-CFT.name: Local reciprocity and local existence theorem
KX-LOCAL-CFT.reference: J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, Chapter I, Theorems 1.1 and 1.4; profinite completion and units/inertia in paragraphs 1.10-1.11.
KX-LOCAL-CFT.precise_input: The topological abelianization of the absolute Galois group of a finite extension K/Q_ell is the profinite completion of K^times, and units correspond to inertia.
KX-LOCAL-CFT.hypothesis_match: K is the completion at the original valuation; source splitting identifies it with F_v. Arithmetic Frobenius normalization is fixed; free/torsion decomposition is proved separately.

KX-CHENEVIER.name: Continuous determinant prorepresentability under Phi_ell

KX-CHENEVIER.precise_input: Continuous determinants deforming a finite-field semisimple residual representation of a profinite group satisfying condition (F) have a complete Noetherian local universal W(k)-algebra.
KX-CHENEVIER.hypothesis_match: GDet is a multiplicative homogeneous polynomial law with full naturality. Condition (F) is exact PhiCond. The residual direct sum is finite and continuous. No residual irreducibility or ell>n assumption is introduced. Actual O extension and degree zero are proved separately.

QX-THORNE.name: Polarized adjoint Bloch--Kato vanishing
QX-THORNE.reference: J.A.Thorne, arXiv:2207.04925, Theorem6.1, printedp24; unitary-adjoint normalization and delta^n epsilon^(1-n) in Section6.3, p25.
QX-THORNE.statement: For an actual regular algebraic cuspidal polarized pair over a CM field and n>=2, irreducibility on the full cyclotomic extension implies vanishing of its polarized adjoint H1_f.
QX-THORNE.matching: QX1 proves surjectivity onto Gamma-prime, actual Frobenius attachment, exact form scalar cancellation and minus-transpose action, finite coefficient capture and original Af.IsBK matching. No residual adequacy or lower bound on ell is inferred.

QX-BLGGT.name: Polarized Galois representations and algebraic Hecke avatars
QX-BLGGT.reference: Barnet-Lamb--Gee--Geraghty--Taylor, Annals179(2014), Theorem2.1.1(1)--(3), printedp538, and AppendixA.2, printedp600.
QX-BLGGT.statement: Actual regular algebraic polarized cusp pairs have continuous semisimple Galois representations with geometric local compatibility away ell and de Rham property. Algebraic ell-adic rank-one characters are the avatars of algebraic Hecke characters, with the explicit infinity/cyclotomic normalization.
QX-BLGGT.matching: QX1 uses the exact CSD polarization. QX7 checks integral local exponents before using rank-one reciprocity. QX9 first constructs and sign-corrects actual polarized pairs; no infinity sign is identified with the uncorrected avatar at complex conjugation.

QX-CHENEVIER.name: Determinants, integral coefficient identities and absolutely irreducible realization
QX-CHENEVIER.reference: G.Chenevier, arXiv:0809.0415v2, Lemma1.12, Corollary1.14, Theorem1.15, Theorem2.22(i), Remark3.5.
QX-CHENEVIER.statement: Integral mixed determinant coefficients are polynomials in group-word characteristic coefficients; a split absolutely irreducible residual Cayley--Hamilton determinant over a henselian ring is a matrix determinant; universal determinant rings are topologically generated by their coefficient functions.
QX-CHENEVIER.matching: QX3 applies to the dual-number point and upgrades weak Pair trace relations by Burnside/Nakayama. QX5 descends the full law integrally, including ell=3. QX3 does not apply B.univ to Qbar[epsilon].

QX-CFT.name: Finite and local class field theory
QX-CFT.reference: J.S.Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03, I Theorems1.1,1.4; V Theorems5.3,5.5 and Remark5.7.
QX-CFT.statement: Local units correspond to inertia; global finite abelian extensions and ray-class characters are given by idele reciprocity with compatible norms and Frobenius.
QX-CFT.matching: QX4 explicitly constructs kappa0 and the one-sided ell-adic character mu using finite ray classes; the root/continuity/parity/threshold calculations are proved. QX7 and QX9 use the original local embeddings and finite coefficient fields.

QX-CHEBOTAREV.name: Chebotarev and semisimple-character comparison
QX-CHEBOTAREV.reference: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem8.31; finite-dimensional semisimple character criterion.
QX-CHEBOTAREV.statement: Each conjugacy class in a finite Galois group occurs at infinitely many unramified primes; continuous semisimple characteristic-zero representations agreeing on a dense Frobenius set are isomorphic.
QX-CHEBOTAREV.matching: QX4 uses a class fixing the original F and K to obtain degree-one split auxiliary primes avoiding any finite set. QX1/QX9 check continuity and semisimplicity before comparison.

QX-AC.name: Cyclic cuspidal base change and descent with strong local compatibility
QX-AC.reference: Arthur--Clozel, Simple Algebras, Base Change, and the Advanced Theory of the Trace Formula, ChapterIII Theorem4.2(a),(b),(d), pp202--203; Theorem5.1, p212; ChapterI Section6, including Theorem6.2.
QX-AC.statement: A Galois-invariant cusp descends through a cyclic prime-degree extension, uniquely up to its finite quotient characters; a cusp base changes cuspidally unless the prescribed quotient self-twist occurs; global base change is strong at every place and compatible with the local correspondence.
QX-AC.matching: Only rank4 cyclic steps are used in QX9. Invariance follows from the actual extended r and strong multiplicity one. Irreducibility and the fresh ramified prime exclude exceptional self-twists. Every finite character ambiguity is corrected before returning the original r.

QX-HLTT.name: Galois existence without a prior polarization
QX-HLTT.reference: Harris--Lan--Taylor--Thorne, On the rigid cohomology of certain Shimura varieties, TheoremA / Corollary7.14.
QX-HLTT.statement: A regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GLn over a CM field has a continuous semisimple Galois representation matching geometric normalized unramified Satake polynomials.
QX-HLTT.matching: Used only after Arthur--Clozel constructs a specific descent cusp. Its restriction is the given irreducible r, so the finite-character discrepancy is explicitly removed. No automorphy of an arbitrary representation is inferred.

QX-CAR.name: Full CSD local compatibility and every-finite-place temperedness
QX-CAR.reference: A.Caraiani, Duke Math.J.161(2012), Theorems1.1--1.2, printedp2312; Monodromy and local-global compatibility for l=p, Theorem1.1 (ANT8(2014)).
QX-CAR.statement: For any n>=2 and actual cohomological conjugate-self-dual CM cusp, full Frobenius-semisimplified local compatibility holds at every finite place, and every finite local component is tempered.
QX-CAR.matching: QX9 applies only to the actual end2 CSD cusp at the chosen CM field, after the regular-algebraic/cohomological match. It then transports essential temperedness through the explicit cyclic chain. No Shin-regularity hypothesis is dropped from a theorem that has one.

QX-BGP.name: Semisimplified local compatibility at ell
QX-BGP.reference: Barnet-Lamb--Gee--Geraghty--Taylor, Local-global compatibility for l=p, II, TheoremA; Theorem1.1 and Corollary1.2.
QX-BGP.statement: At ell, the semisimplified Weil representation attached to an actual regular algebraic polarized CM cusp agrees with geometric local Langlands. Full Frobenius-semisimplification in this theorem has a further Shin-regularity condition.
QX-BGP.matching: QX9 uses only the first conclusion. Its equation QX.26 and literal Unl1 rule out norm-ratio monodromy entries, so N=0 is proved independently, then temperedness gives PotUnl and WinAt.

QX-CLOZEL.name: Regular algebraic cuspidal representations are cohomological
QX-CLOZEL.reference: L.Clozel, Motifs et formes automorphes (1990), Lemma3.14, with Theorem3.13; already matched in CX-CL.
QX-CLOZEL.statement: A regular C-algebraic cuspidal representation of GLn has nonzero relative Lie algebra cohomology with the algebraic coefficient of the same infinitesimal character.
QX-CLOZEL.matching: Matches the source IsRegAlg of the actual CSD cusp to Caraiani's cohomological premise. Only this archimedean consequence is reused; no counting or rationality bound is used.

QX-LINEAR.name: Finite-dimensional density, Clifford theory and elementary character independence
QX-LINEAR.reference: P.Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, Theorem2.5(i), p24; elementary proofs of the needed finite-index and self-twist cases are supplied in QX8--QX9.
QX-LINEAR.statement: A finite-dimensional irreducible representation over an algebraically closed field spans the full endomorphism algebra; distinct one-dimensional characters are linearly independent.
QX-LINEAR.matching: Burnside gives the trace-coordinate and weak-relation upgrades. QX8 proves the exact rank4 char-ell N3 argument, including characteristic3, rather than importing a stronger residual-image theorem.

QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.name: Noetherian local dimension and going-down facts
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.reference: Normal-domain going-down for integral extensions, the equality of regular-local dimension and cotangent dimension, and Krull intersection; the finite-point and formal-series comparison is already DX5.
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.statement: Integral finite domain extensions of a normal domain satisfy going-down; dimension is at most embedding dimension; equality characterizes a regular local ring, which is a domain; ideals of a complete Noetherian local ring are closed.
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.matching: QX2 uses normality of the actual regular weight ring and torsion-freeness before applying the dimension bound. It proves the support conclusion by localization. QX6 takes closed-ideal limits only in the complete Noetherian ring B.

external_literature.author: W. Banaszczyk
external_literature.title: New bounds in some transference theorems in the geometry of numbers
external_literature.primary_text_retrieval: Original paper transcription, section 2, Theorem (2.1), printed p.631; publisher metadata independently checked. The primary text includes the n=1 equality case.
external_literature.statement_used: For every full Euclidean lattice M in R^n, λ_i(M) λ_{n+1−i}(M*) ≤ n; only i=n is used.
hypothesis_match: M is the original Hermitian dual L_c^vee embedded in S tensor_Q R; n=[E:Q]k.
B(x,y)=Tr_{E/Q} h_S(x,y) is real symmetric positive definite, by CM trace invariance and original ColVal positivity.
L_c^vee is a full finitely generated Z-lattice, hence discrete and spans the Euclidean space.
Integer-pairing dual M* is exactly D_E^(-1)L_c, with no factor two in B.
For nonzero z in M*, h(z,z) lies in D_E^(-2); ideal norm and AM–GM give λ_1(M*) ≥ sqrt([E:Q])/rd(E).
Result gives k E-independent y_a in the original L_c^vee with Tr h(y_a,y_a)/(2f) ≤ k^2(2v)^2.
external_literature.not_claimed: The chapter does not reconstruct Banaszczyk's Gaussian transference proof; this is an explicit category A import.
external_literature.application_scope: Any original ColVal D u and any original level-zero class c, before family, word, or place thresholds are introduced.
original_source_facts: ColVal supplies the original full class lattice L_c, its positive definite Hermitian form, and LatT integrality.
The original host has [E:Q]=2f and v=rd(E)/2; no redefinition of either normalization is made.
The target ShortAt bound is Tr h(y_a,y_a)/(2f) <= k^2(2v)^2 for k E-independent vectors in L_c^vee.
independently_derived_normalization: For B=Tr h the integer-pairing dual of L_c^vee is D_E^(-1)L_c, since h is Hermitian and the codifferent is stable under CM conjugation.
If z is nonzero in that trace dual, beta=h(z,z) is totally positive and belongs to D_E^(-2); therefore |Norm beta| disc(E)^2 >= 1.
AM–GM gives B(z,z)>= [E:Q]/rd(E)^2, and hence lambda_1(M*)>=sqrt([E:Q])/rd(E).
The published inequality in dimension n=[E:Q]k gives lambda_n(M)^2 <= [E:Q] k^2 rd(E)^2.
Extracting k E-independent vectors and dividing by [E:Q]=2f yields the exact source target, with rd(E)=2v and no extra factor two or T.

claims.title: All selected normal prefix types inherit the original maximum-weight cutoffs
claims.status: proved_specialization_of_characteristic_zero_representation_theory
claims.statement: Canonical isotypic projectors for nested/disjoint prefixes commute. Joint-isotypic vectors span each finite-degree space, so the literal IsJProj condition determines the product projector uniquely. A nonzero selected normal vector therefore has each selected type present; its largest coordinate is bounded by the original segment normal-prefix maximum. No integral direct sum or projector-denominator estimate is used.
claims.background: Ordinary characteristic-zero complete reducibility and highest-weight extremal-weight facts, already used in v0_5 PG/IW. The report supplies the precise commutation, uniqueness, homogeneous-filtering and prefix identification argument.

claims.title: Weighted Fock lattices, algebraic orders and actual cutoff projectors
claims.statement: The lattice b(F)>=0 is full, torus-graded and divided-power stable for arbitrary ramification, by the half-sum of two binomial valuations. Apply the companion IW4 to the S-letter weight interval [-D_S,D_S], using the difference of the same coordinate in two weights <=2D_S. The cutoff ord_S>=theta is the sum of isotypic components with last highest weight>=ceil(theta). Its Fock projector is selfadjoint; nested/disjoint cutoff projectors commute. Rescaling by p^ceil(-b(F)) gives weighted loss<=r^2(log_p(2T+r)+1). The V2 order calculus and binomial-operator degree costs are proved directly.

claims.title: The joint chain projector has controlled coefficients and preserves every label/tangent block
claims.statement: Form the product of the weakened chain cutoff projectors. Its sets are nested within segments, disjoint across segments, and contained in or disjoint from every relevant link set. It therefore preserves links. Euler commutation fixes every outside label/tangent exponent. On good x^zeta it has b>=v_p(zeta!)/2-Dm; within the resulting block factorial valuations differ by at most kp, so all coefficients are >=-Dm-kp/2. Hence p^ceil(Dm+kp/2) clears its coefficients on integral good inputs.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.

The original CNL domain, injective coefficient embedding and all ten WtRep assertion fields are retained. The actual control formula, positive operators, sufficiently deep classical levels and finite away sums are compatible.

Its original Hecke algebra is finite complete local with the prescribed residue field, and all positive generators are units. Domain is used only for the printed torsion-freeness conclusion.

They prove dyadic separation, finite-coefficient continuity, the exact local tangent-to-Bloch–Kato comparison, and the original epsilon^-1 twist and full M3 polarization P=J. Arbitrary local A->O, potentially noninjective/nonflat from a nonreduced source, is retained; O and its specified target embedding have the original hypotheses.

They capture the given arithmetic point in one actual finite coefficient DVR with uniform ideal-power decay; identify the local coefficient map, finite-part character, depth shift, literal ClAt/OrdAt spaces, all local and spherical normalizations; and install one specialization map across every level, basis, operator and auxiliary action. KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.
SP-C1.matching: Applied only to finite O modules whose finiteness is proved in the chapter. SP1 handles additive, not assumed O-linear, injections through finite cardinality. SP6 proves the norm-weighted length formula from these finite module facts.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C1.name: Noetherian formal series, complete quotients and henselian finite algebras
IX-C1.statement_used: Finite formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; quotients of a complete Noetherian local ring remain complete; a finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a finite product of local rings, so a finite domain is local.
IX-C1.matching: Used on the actual IsCO rings, the finite eigenvalue algebra C[b], and complete prime quotients. Integrality makes the origin evaluation land in O; uniqueness of the maximal ideal proves localness before reducing quotient labels. Successive approximation arguments are given directly.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion
IX-C2.statement_used: A locally projective morphism is proper; a quasi-compact morphism is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.
IX-C2.source: Stacks Project, Lemma29.44.5 tag01WC and Proposition26.20.6 tag01KF.
IX-C2.matching: The symplectic flag variety is explicitly a closed incidence/isotropy subvariety of a product of Grassmannians. The schematic closure of the actual generic flag is proper and surjects the integral base. A chosen K-point then extends over the given valuation ring. This does not assume smoothness, flatness or uniqueness of flags.

IX-C3.name: Weak Nullstellensatz
IX-C3.statement_used: Every nonzero finite-type algebra over an algebraically closed field has a rational closed point.
IX-C3.matching: Applied only to the nonzero finite-type invariant fibre. Nonzero follows from the weight-zero retraction before field extension. Full formal evaluation is justified separately using positive valuations and finite monomial decompositions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.
IX-C4.matching: Captures finitely many algebraic flag-basis entries in a single complete DVR inside the original V. Equal-characteristic purely inseparable extensions are handled separately by adjoining ell-power roots of a uniformizer over the perfect finite residue field; Milne is not misquoted as already proving that part.

IX-C5.name: Minkowski: no nontrivial everywhere-finite-unramified extension of Q
IX-C5.statement_used: A finite extension of Q unramified at every finite prime is Q.
IX-C5.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorem4.9, printedp72/PDFpage74.
IX-C5.matching: Applied to each finite continuous reduction of a powered character. The character is first shown trivial on every original inertia group, including ell. Separatedness is used only after these finite assertions. No assertion about arbitrary infinite unramified extensions is used.

IX-C6.name: Density theorem over an algebraically closed field
IX-C6.statement_used: The image of an algebra in the endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional simple module over an algebraically closed field is the full endomorphism algebra.
IX-C6.source: P.Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, January10,2011, Theorem2.5(i), p24; Section2.5 finite-dimensional algebra proof.
IX-C6.matching: Used only to turn simplicity on G_L back into the literal matrix-span Irr predicate. The finite-index semisimplicity, self-twist construction, injective characteristic-zero transport and distinct residual-character contradiction are proved in IX10.

The proof checks every Teichmuller lift, every weaker IsRecT map, all allowed residue primes including 3, repeated inertia characters and arbitrary nonzero individually isotypic product modules. A matched crystalline inertial-type theorem supplies the local complex detector. Integer norm exponents make its detecting property invariant under coefficient conjugation; a stable lattice followed by restriction of scalars returns the final representation to the original O. The inherited local Langlands and RecTExists foundations are explicitly retained. Substitution into OTW13/CAP17 gives the original HdEx/UnitaryHeckeData.

Finite class representatives make the actual definite unitary quotient compact and its original invariant form positive; checked finite multiplicity and algebraic semisimplicity give finite equivariant projections. Exact bidual scalarization preserves the prescribed basis, infinity representation, rational equivariance and all matrix-valued coefficient equations. This constructs the actual automorphic decomposition, while its Galois decoration remains separate.

CFD1–CFD12 prove full original clParts_alt and a predicate refinement. Finite left-coset averaging works without normal stabilizers, preserves every original compact scalar profile, and keeps the same level, depth and finite-part characters. Polynomial projectors preserve the original norm-one generalized eigenspaces of the normalized Uz. The original AutomorphicHeckeSet premise is retained, rather than inferred from decompU alone.

AFS1–AFS22 prove the domain and full DenseWt statements on every supplied original LamObj, exact arithmetic/good-point equivalence, occurrence of every specified Hecke character in the faithful module fiber without flatness, the original distinct-unit principal-series criterion and goodScalB_alt, full partAct0_alt and TCoreSep/Out.sep. The same-kernel argument proves density for the very same IsJ ideal when the exact original AutomorphicHeckeSet supplier is present. Nonzero-block fiber nonvanishing is proved; existence of a nonzero block for an arbitrary residual label is not asserted.

FLC1–FLC19 prove the full original root-injectivity collision estimate with constant 23, the exact finite pattern exchange and lower character law, the squarefree Gelfand–Graev weight formula, and transfer to the unchanged normalized polynomial labels. Green’s cuspidal theorem is the one explicit published finite-group input, with its primary-symbol and degree/value dictionary. KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.

version_0_45_local_conclusions: HED1-HED16 prove the literal arithmetic-point decomposition/end1 on the given representation. Surjective quotient factorization keeps the original point and weight; full polynomial-law naturality keeps all scalar algebras. One HalfG seed is chosen for every original cusp and every positive Speh length, and the exact inverse cyclotomic strings are retained. Degree-one Chebotarev turns their Frobenius product into a global characteristic-polynomial identity.
