HAW1-HAW19 prove the full original automorphy-away/end2 endpoint. They compare the arbitrary supplied representation with the actual automorphic part, extract ordinary principal-series data at every arithmetic point without a Good guard, and prove the ordered flag and conjugate-place transport. A single global unitarizing norm twist gives one real window center before all eligible places. The exact ordinary-character calculation shows that any positive-power cyclotomic ratio forces a forbidden factor q between the two complex character norms. This proves the full AutOffN predicate with conditional continuity precisely where the source places it.

HPT1-HPT18 prove the all-positive-rank ordinary return UpUW and the entire PointTheoremBaseObject field with its original rank 2 through 4 antecedent. The proof reconstructs a nonzero actual automorphic part, its integral type and original residual block, then shows that the resulting Hecke point is the given point by the universal-ring property over a finite coefficient ring. Thus it concludes J is contained in the given point kernel; it does not assume this. The exact DescWeak foundation remains explicit only where the low-rank point theorem uses it.

HTS1-HTS8 prove the original TwistOk in every positive rank on the same J. An odd-order conjugate-dual Galois character has a square-root power, which gives the actual adelic unitary determinant twist. Its split local character is the required square. Multiplication by this character preserves the original infinity weights, outside-place unramifiedness and depth-one vector. Full determinant laws and the guarded local comparisons give every input of HPT17 for the twisted point. The argument includes ell=3 and does not import the low-rank DescWeak premise into the all-rank twisting theorem.

HLM1-HLM26 construct the full original LevelAlt with one base before every auxiliary level, including the empty set. An integral trace criterion gives projectivity without division by the quotient-group order. The actual directed union has exactly the required fixed modules and one coherent universal-ring action. At each level the determinant is first constructed over the integral Hecke algebra by compact interpolation and integral word identities; its full ordinary pair gives the surjective universal map. Classical points separate module vectors, and the old-level identification preserves the same support ideal and every original local correspondence quantifier.

HTW1-HTW24 reconstruct the full level-to-Taylor-Wiles consumer. The tame Hecke relation retains its diagonal-unit terms, and a Jacquet dimension bound gives the uniform exponent n!. Explicit integral divided-difference dual families construct both comparison maps; their compositions are enlarged to exactly the original ordered-pair fEl. A canonical topologically nilpotent summand is projective, hence free, over the local diamond group algebra. Completed ordered-root and coefficient maps preserve both full trace relations and the exact theta_coefficientMap_eq. One base, one prior root lift, and one exponent then work for every auxiliary N, giving the same-J HasAut.

HIA1-HIA6 assemble the complete original HidaUAlt and perform the selected rank-four support installation. The empty-level IsJ supplies one ideal carrying all six Hida fields and HasAut. The inherited selected patching, normalization, pro-ell and P1 consumers apply to that same ideal. KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.

version_0_47_local_conclusions: KTR reconstructs the full original KatoUse, KatoTwo and RigII. Kato Theorem14.2(1) is applied at weight2e+1 and twist e, with the paper's Bcris/unramified conditions and inverse-arithmetic-Frobenius polynomial checked directly. The actual local point gives the needed inertia flag from ordIdeal contained in It; prime-to-ell inertia and the class-number condition kill the middle and determinant characters. The corner extension is explicit and irreducible on the full infinite cyclotomic kernel. Actual quadratic GL2 base change and its symmetric polarization supply Thorne's corner-adjoint vanishing. Concrete projections decompose all nine adjoint coordinates into that corner, W, W times the quadratic character, and the quadratic scalar line, producing the required primitive for every original cocycle. The original modularity antecedent is retained.

KIZ supplies the entire original CohInp/InpZ record from the completed exact human inputs. It preserves the local period model, normalized finite cohomology, original uniform LemmaK constant and every later coefficient datum, and inserts the completed LemmaM/LemmaMprime/LemmaP, KTR RigII, AdVanishK and RNC congruence integer at their literal fields. The independent original OneChar and AutomorphyUnramifiedCoefficients producers remain open.

RFD proves the full original RowsFinDim with arbitrary locally constant supported e, arbitrary original unit vectors, and all original measures and weak integral operators. One compact-open level is chosen from e. The exact adelic quotient splits into finitely many arithmetic real components; the matched Harish-Chandra finite-multiplicity theorem applies there. The Schur projector's compression identity gives an explicit injection from its range into bounded intertwiners. This proves finite dimensionality without adding idempotence, smoothness, compact-finiteness, gap or cuspidality assumptions.

ASG constructs eight actual dependent blocks of the original adelic setting: unitary instance, integral lattice/flags, finite character, reference frame, transport matrices, automorphic bundle, finite representation block, and subgroup/quotient measures. The original Forms0 produces an extra isotropic vector. Steinitz decomposition and a trace-one triangular correction give the prescribed integral hyperbolic frame; an explicit ideal-class/primitive-vector argument supplies all negative word vectors and every FixedHyp field. Split finite-adeles prove full generic ScRefExists and ScXuExists even for arbitrary supplied reference frames. Original gap and earlier discrete-series decay supply the full bundle. The original Bessel W, measured-field, Siegel-Weil ties, arithmetic count and common-family producers remain explicit.

CNC constructs the entire original IsNab connection over every original coefficient algebra, including nonreduced and nonlocal rings. The full tangent eigenframe gives compatible global formal jets; normalized rigidified generators and proper base functions give every biextension law. A formal logarithm, two explicit symmetric-cocycle primitives, a separability-idempotent correction and the antisymmetric half correction prove the full generic canonical-gauge theorem. Unique germs of all sections give exactly the original nabVal formula. This removes the separate IsNab input from the ICL lattice-spanning route; principal-chart existence, finite theta systems and the other named spanning producers remain distinct.

PCL constructs the exact original Hermitian-coordinate and trace-dual cusp-lattice data, and the quantitative DataX normalization on each supplied principal chart. Its explicit fractional-ideal and different calculation preserves the original fields, lattice, metric, scalar and denominator conventions. The prescribed half-different and quadratic ideal norm give the host identity and exact NA/NC and logarithmic bounds. IsUnf, HasPrinc/GamAt, LawsCore and actual common uniformization remain original antecedents; this is not a new claim of their existence.

LGS supplies the actual local-growth, canonical mean-deficit and full admission inputs for the original local-gain route. It proves the required small-order and band bounds, local lattice projection/walk estimates and normalized lengths, then changes only the auxiliary Ch field to zero and verifies every field of that admitted record. The original valuation lattices, comparison maps, degree data, supports and family are unchanged. All five LinkG conclusions follow with exactly C_G=4C_count+1 and b_o=b^(x^(-epsilon/2)). The pointwise LinkG theorem retains actual GroupCompatibilityFamily and Adm2F on the same family; actual TopsF supplies Adm2F. The exact class-level linkG_concrete5 retains the two corresponding Closed predicates, with their cutoffs and coefficient bounds chosen before the family, in addition to the original ambient family bounds.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.
SP-C1.matching: Applied only to finite O modules whose finiteness is proved in the chapter. SP1 handles additive, not assumed O-linear, injections through finite cardinality. SP6 proves the norm-weighted length formula from these finite module facts.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion
IX-C2.statement_used: A locally projective morphism is proper; a quasi-compact morphism is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.
IX-C2.source: Stacks Project, Lemma29.44.5 tag01WC and Proposition26.20.6 tag01KF.

The schematic closure of the actual generic flag is proper and surjects the integral base. A chosen K-point then extends over the given valuation ring. IX-C3.name: Weak Nullstellensatz

IX-C3.matching: Applied only to the nonzero finite-type invariant fibre. Nonzero follows from the weight-zero retraction before field extension. Full formal evaluation is justified separately using positive valuations and finite monomial decompositions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.

IX-C5.name: Minkowski: no nontrivial everywhere-finite-unramified extension of Q

IX-C5.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorem4.9, printedp72/PDFpage74.
IX-C5.matching: Applied to each finite continuous reduction of a powered character. The character is first shown trivial on every original inertia group, including ell. Separatedness is used only after these finite assertions. No assertion about arbitrary infinite unramified extensions is used.

IX-C6.name: Density theorem over an algebraically closed field

version_0_49_local_conclusions: UCE reconstructs the full original local ordinary-point and coefficient-algebra path. Finite weight zero then controls arbitrary entry-algebra maps through finite homogeneous modules, rather than presuming their continuity. Every point has an actual finite-coefficient ordinary torus conjugate, and TypeI is irreducible on every required open subgroup. Conjugacy transports both exact automorphic conclusions and every outer-corner extension at the same fixed iota. Thus one common GdEnd supplies FinA, AutB and LemW for one shared g1. GdEnd itself, the common abelian-CM frame, both seeds and full PfromAut/ModUAlt remain explicit; AUT_UNRAM_COEF is not closed.

BWP reconstructs the actual local wave packet and its normalized global product. An explicit polynomial chart on the original unipotent group has Haar Jacobian one and yields the exact integrable norm exponent. Harish-Chandra admissibility and a finite-dimensional convolution-polynomial argument give the full compact reproducer in any prescribed identity neighborhood. The original cubic GapBig dominates every required decay exponent and proves the whole CoefWeightedLoc for every supplied discrete series and lowest unit vector. The packet is continuous, equivariant, has the printed weighted quotient L1 and L2 bounds, and is reproduced by the exact formal-degree kernel and a compact kernel. The retained BesselNVGap gives precisely its nonzero norm, so the original WlocExists is complete on its original antecedents. Correct transport uses two group conjugacies and one equivariant torsor map, preserves the character factor4*pi/g_D and every supplied measure, and gives WFromLoc plus WExists conditional on BesselNVGap. The global vector is chosen before every later measured block and satisfies its decay. With inherited Forms0 setting blocks this gives ConcreteSettingExists in their original scope. BesselNVGap, multiplicity-one and the later orbital/Siegel-Weil comparisons remain separate.

HUF supplies the whole original finite holomorphic FamilyUnif and N1c on the given Moduli record. It extracts the actual exponential kernel, integral CM datum and all-level Tate/genus comparisons from every moduli point; constructs relative exponentials and full continued lattices; and proves the prescribed local lift on one neighborhood with every positive Weil level. Period kernel coordinates and marked uniqueness prove holomorphy even for arbitrary pointwise choices of points and exponentials. Finitely many analytic components give one finite positive family chosen before all periods and bases, without compactness of the moduli space. Explicit primitive semicharacters give fixed half characteristics and theta factors. Proper analytic base change and the zero rigidification provide the global normalized theta-line isomorphism; projective GAGA supplies the algebraic section on each fiber. Every FamilyUnif and IsThetaFrame clause, exact negative Weil sign, both markings, dimension-zero case and universal choice order is retained. The representing Moduli itself, principal framed points, IsUnf, reduced-test FromTest and later theta spanning remain adjoining producers.

WRS supplies the full uniform local-gain selected obligation. The complete local/Taylor kernel and comparison record survives division on arbitrary original submodules, and one map on the dependent joint tuple preserves the actual geometric kernel. Membership in the original built class already identifies the given point and Extra data with a joint constructed witness. This yields GroupCompatibilityFamily after one family threshold without a new selector premise. Existing D3 ChosenE gives selected tops and Adm2F. The completed LGS13 implication therefore gives all five original LinkG_at fields with CG=4*Ccount+1 and delta(x)=x^(-epsilon/2), chosen before all later actual indices. The original universal TSel/Duty installer is also proved. GLOBAL_LOCAL_GAIN is closed; the historical stronger WPt/TSel construction is not declared solved, and common-family nonemptiness plus the separate denominator, period-height, spectral and second-layer producers remain open.

KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.
SP-C1.matching: Applied only to finite O modules whose finiteness is proved in the chapter. SP1 handles additive, not assumed O-linear, injections through finite cardinality. SP6 proves the norm-weighted length formula from these finite module facts.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields

KB-C1.name: Quillen finite generation and canonical K-theory model
KB-C1.statement_used: For every number field L, K_i(O_L) is finitely generated for all i>=0. The standard Quillen K-groups for i>=1 are pi_i(BGL_infinity(O_L)^+).
KB-C1.source: D. Quillen, Finite generation of the groups K_i of rings of algebraic integers, LNM341 (1973),179-198,Theorem1; canonical plus/exact-category comparison in Quillen K-theory, also Arlettaz Definition3.12 and Remark3.16.
KB-C1.matching: O_L is the full ring of integers, m=2e>=2. Finite generation at m-1 is also used for the finite-coefficient inverse limit. Only the canonical model is chosen; no universal assertion for arbitrary source Plus records is inferred.

KB-C2.name: Borel even-degree rank zero
KB-C2.statement_used: For number fields and i>=2, rank K_i(O_L) is 0,r1+r2,0,r2 according to i mod4=0,1,2,3; only the even zero cases are used.
KB-C2.source: A. Borel, Stable real cohomology of arithmetic groups, Ann.Sci.ENS7(1974),235-272,Proposition12.2,p.271.
KB-C2.matching: Set D=k=L in the proposition for orders in central division algebras, and the order to O_L. Together with KB-C1 gives finiteness, not merely torsion.

KB-C3.kind: named classical citation leaf, matched in finite coefficients
KB-C3.name: Dwyer-Friedlander finite coefficient comparison and etale spectral sequence
KB-C3.statement_used: For a field of ell-cohomological dimension at most2, or its ring of S-integers, finite-coefficient algebraic-to-etale K comparison is onto in degrees>=2; for ell2 use r>=2 and a primitive fourth root. Localizing at ell does not change these algebraic K groups with finite ell-power coefficients in degrees>=2. The finite etale spectral sequence has E2^{p,-q}=H^p_et(U,Z/ell^r(q/2)), even q, converging to K_{q-p}^et.
KB-C3.source: W.G.Dwyer and E.M.Friedlander, Algebraic and etale K-theory, Trans.AMS292(1985),247-280,Propositions5.2,8.1,8.2 and Theorem8.5; completed conclusion Theorem8.7 and Remark8.8.
KB-C3.matching: Total complexness supplies finite ell-cd through LD3; HasMuQ supplies integral primitive fourth root at ell2. The proof handles m2 explicitly with finite comparison, avoiding any OCR ambiguity in Theorem8.7. Cofinal r>=2 at ell2. Compatible maps pass through exact finite systems, with all limit arguments given in KB1-2.

KB-C4.name: Finite etale/Galois comparison and finiteness
KB-C4.statement_used: For U=Spec O_L[1/ell], locally constant finite ell-primary sheaves have G_S cohomology equal to etale cohomology and all finite-level groups are finite.
KB-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems,2nded(2006),II Proposition2.9 and Theorem2.13. Global higher vanishing is already LD3 (I Theorem4.10).
KB-C4.matching: ell is invertible on U. The original closed-inertia quotient is pi1(U); original D.chi is the uniquely descended cyclotomic character. The compact integral comparison is proved here, not included in this finite theorem.

KB-C5.name: Van der Kallen integral homology stability
KB-C5.statement_used: With stable dimension d and a>=2m+max(1,d), H_m(GL_a(R),Z)->H_m(GL_{a+1}(R),Z) is an isomorphism.
KB-C5.source: W.van der Kallen, Homology stability for linear groups,Invent.Math.60(1980),269-295,Convention2.2 and Theorem4.11,p.289.
KB-C5.matching: KB3 proves source StableRangeLe O_L2 by CRT, which is SR3 and permits d=1 in Convention2.2. The actual block inclusions at a>=N=2m+4 are well within the integral range. Bar homology commuting with filtered unions is proved.

KB-C6.name: Arlettaz integral Hurewicz kernel bound
KB-C6.statement_used: For any ring and m>=2, R_m kills the kernel of K_m(R)->H_m(GL_infinity(R),Z), where R_m=product_{a=2}^m L_a and L_a is squarefree.
KB-C6.source: D.Arlettaz, Algebraic K-theory of rings from a topological viewpoint,PublicacionsMatematiques44(2000),3-84,Definitions7.11,7.14 and Corollary7.19(a),pp.52-55.
KB-C6.matching: Target is GL, not E. Source ArlAdm/arlL/arlR agree after zero-versus-one sequence reindexing; cutoff p<=a loses no prime, L1=1. Flat base change preserves kernel, v_ell R_m<=m-1<=cOne(m), unit part invertible. No omitted small primes.

KB-C7.name: Unramified global Artin reciprocity
KB-C7.statement_used: The Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of L unramified at all places is the ordinary ideal class group.
KB-C7.matching: Strict Sha characters vanish on original decomposition groups above ell, are unramified elsewhere by GS, and L has no real places. They therefore inject into Hom(Cl(O_L),F_ell), whose order is at most classNumber L.

KB-C8.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
KB-C8.statement_used: Each ideal class has an integral representative of norm <=(n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrtDelta.
KB-C8.matching: KB7 proves the prefactor<=1, bounds ideal counts by d_n and sums these counts, deriving log h_L<=n logDelta/2 and the exact source generator constant4.

KB-C9.name: Henselization/completion finite separable extension equivalence
KB-C9.statement_used: The henselization selected by an original finite-place valuation of a global field is excellent; completion preserves its category of finite separable extensions and Galois groups.
KB-C9.source: J.S.Milne,ArithmeticDualityTheorems,2nded(2006),I AppendixA,Case2,pp.130-131; classical Krasner finite-extension comparison, also the setup of LD3.
KB-C9.matching: Keep D.A_v. Its decomposition group is the Galois group of the selected henselization. Embed its completion L_v as a finite intermediate K_v inside PadicAlgCl(ell). The resulting continuous Galois isomorphism preserves every root-of-unity action, and precomposition transports cochains, cups and original restrictions. This matches the exact decompositionGroup_mulEquiv_localGalois_cyclotomic statement.

SP-C1.name: DVR/PID module structure and Smith bases
SP-C1.statement_used: Finite torsion-free modules over a DVR are free; finite modules decompose into free and cyclic torsion parts; full-rank submodules admit Smith bases and determinant gives their index.
SP-C1.source: Keith Conrad, Modules over a PID, Corollary2.6, Theorem4.1, Section4 aligned bases and Theorem5.22.

SP-C2.name: Noetherian prime filtration
SP-C2.statement_used: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a finite filtration with quotients R/p; the graded refinement is obtained by choosing homogeneous annihilators.
SP-C2.matching: SP2 explains the homogeneous refinement and proves the specific Euler nonnegativity argument; no positivity theorem is left as an unexplained citation.

SP-C3.name: Nullstellensatz, Nakayama and finite etale algebras over a field
SP-C3.statement_used: Maximal residue fields of finite-type algebras over algebraically closed K equal K; radical ideals are intersections of maximal ideals. For a finite local module M=mM implies M=0. Finite etale field algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions.
SP-C3.matching: SP3 base changes the nonzero finite-type algebra ((A/J_epsilon) tensor_B Frac(B/p))[1/q], never an arbitrary transcendental residue field. SP4 uses zero cotangent at all closed points and characteristic zero to prove the finite-etale slice, then gives an explicit double cover.

SP-C4.name: Bertrand prime theorem
SP-C4.statement_used: For n>1 there is a prime n<p<2n.
SP-C4.source: P.Erdos, Beweis eines Satzes von Tschebyschef, ActaSciMath(Szeged)5(1932),194-198.
SP-C4.matching: Applied at n=ell*h.N*p1+5; yields source pZero<=2ell*h.N*p1+10, with p>=5, p not dividing level or D.S.

SP-C5.kind: matched elementary local and cyclotomic number theory
SP-C5.name: Unramified Frobenius and cyclotomic value
SP-C5.statement_used: At a finite rational prime p the decomposition group modulo inertia is procyclic, generated by arithmetic Frobenius; roots of unity of order prime to p are unramified and Frobenius acts by the p-th power.
SP-C5.source: J.S.Milne, AlgebraicNumberTheory,v3.08(2020), Chapters6 and8 (cyclotomic extensions, decomposition/inertia and Frobenius); original-place transport also established in KB6.
SP-C5.matching: SP7 retains all original valuation subrings in UnrT; SP10 uses arithmetic Frobenius chi(Fr)=p, and computes H1_unr(E/O(theta)) directly as (E/O)/(theta(Fr)-1)(E/O), hence zero for finite character times a strictly negative twist.

MX-C1.name: Finite unramified extensions and decomposition modulo inertia
MX-C1.statement_used: For a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field, finite unramified extensions correspond to finite residue extensions; the inertia quotient is the residue Galois group. Passing to compatible finite extensions gives procyclic quotient generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
MX-C1.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08, Proposition7.50, Corollary7.52, Remark7.53 and subsequent finite-residue discussion, Theorem7.58(a).
MX-C1.matching: Used only on the chosen original D.pl(q). KB6 supplies henselization/completion equivalence and inertia/cochain compatibility. Conjugacy of places is used on finite normal extensions and passed through their inverse limit; no new place or field is substituted.

MX-C2.name: Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, finite-normal-subgroup specialization
MX-C2.statement_used: For finite G and normal N, group cohomology has the cochain-filtration spectral sequence with E2(p,q)=H^p(G/N,H^q(N,V)). When order(N) is invertible on V, averaging kills all positive q and inflation identifies cohomology with that of G/N on V^N.
MX-C2.source: G.Hochschild and J.-P.Serre, Cohomology of group extensions, Trans.Amer.Math.Soc.74(1953),110-134, ChapterII Theorems1-2, especially printed p125.
MX-C2.matching: MX2 proves the passage through finite continuous cochains and the cyclic H2 vanishing directly. I/N is finite of order prime to ell; coefficients are the exact finite residual-adjoint module tensor the small kernel. No unrelated pro-ell duality or local smoothness theorem is substituted.

MX-C3.name: Noetherian formal power series and complete local quotients
MX-C3.statement_used: Finite-variable formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; a quotient of a complete Noetherian local ring by a proper ideal is complete Noetherian local. Krull intersection is zero for powers of a proper ideal on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring.
MX-C3.source: Stacks Project, Lemma10.31.2 tag0306; Lemma10.160.2 tag0325; Lemma10.51.4 tag00IP.
MX-C3.matching: Applied to the explicit finite formal-series cover and proper quotients whose origins survive. In MX2 a descending chain of subspaces of the finite small kernel stabilizes, and Krull intersection makes its stable term zero. FP1 already provides the automatic continuity and IsCO conventions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.
